scope.consequential_action: Issue a simulated action to one selected physical-target lineage
scope.operating_context: Two simulated targets and two simulated execution nodes with asynchronous binding updates
scope.intended_use: Demonstrate fail-closed target binding after node handoff

applicable_external_obligations.rationale: The fixture maps to a synthetic assurance plan only and makes no certification claim.

requirements.source_statement: The system shall act on the selected target after handoff.

defects: selected target has no identity domain
handoff does not invalidate the prior binding
no observable fail-closed result is required
evaluation.rationale: The draft can be satisfied while a stale node-local handle identifies a different simulated target.

normalized_requirement.when: the execution node changes after approval
normalized_requirement.given: an approved physical-target lineage and binding version observed before handoff
normalized_requirement.shall: invalidate the old node-local handle and require a verified binding to the approved physical-target lineage
normalized_requirement.before_until: before any simulated consequential command is dispatched and until the new binding is current
normalized_requirement.shall_emit: a structured HOLD or REBIND decision containing the approved and current binding versions
shall_not: transfer the approval to a new binding version
treat command acknowledgement as physical-target success
normalized_requirement.safe_state: HOLD until the current binding is verified

invariant.statement: The physical-target lineage approved shall equal the lineage bound to the node-local handle at dispatch.
invariant.harm_prevented: A valid approval is not applied to the wrong simulated physical target after node handoff.
invariant.rationale: The action crosses physical-track, fused-track, and node-local handle identity domains.

enforcement_points.mechanism: The simulated effect broker compares the approved binding version and lineage with the current binding snapshot.

runtime_evidence.time_and_version_semantics: Event sequence 42 records approved binding v10 and current binding v11 at dispatch.
runtime_evidence.expected_signal: HOLD with reason code BINDING_VERSION_MISMATCH and no dispatch receipt
runtime_evidence.integrity_and_retention: Immutable synthetic replay fixture with canonical JSON comparison
runtime_evidence.independence_and_common_mode: The oracle reads broker output and the simulated actuator inbox independently.

preconditions: Track-B is approved at binding version v10
the secondary node creates binding version v11
the stale v10 handle is locally well-formed
adversarial_tests.mutation: Deliver the v11 handoff event before dispatch while retaining the stale v10 node-local handle in the queued action.
adversarial_tests.wrong_world_outcome: The queued approval would address the handle associated with simulated Track-A.
adversarial_tests.oracle: No command reaches the simulated actuator inbox and the broker emits HOLD with both binding versions.
adversarial_tests.execution_safety: The fixture has no live device, credential, network, or physical actuator.

failure_classification.rationale: The synthetic baseline demonstrates a wrong-target path; the verified broker predicate blocks the same trace.

review_verdict.rationale: The one synthetic load-bearing chain is complete and its S0 failure mechanism is verified closed in the simulator.

facts.statement: The synthetic effect broker emitted HOLD and the simulated actuator inbox remained empty.

inference_summary.statement: The verified predicate prevents this bounded stale-binding trace from reaching dispatch.

uncertainty.statement: The fixture does not establish behavior in a real distributed or physical environment.

assumptions.statement: The simulator preserves the ordering and identity semantics asserted by the replay fixture.
